mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, leading to increased borrowing costs and reduced corporate earnings, which in turn results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during tightening cycles.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over three months indicates strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns in periods of RSAFS growth are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within two months signals a tightening labor market, which increases wage costs and reduces corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of UNRATE decrease.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% within a month signals increased economic activity and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of INDPRO increase.

mechanism_narrative: A joint increase in housing starts (HOUST) and real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 5% each within three months signals a strong demand environment, boosting corporate earnings and leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS increase > 5% each in 3 months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of joint HOUST and RSAFS increase.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% within two months signals deflationary pressure, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of CPIAUCSL decrease.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payroll employment (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 jobs within a month signals a strong labor market, which increases consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of PAYEMS increase.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in GDP (GDPC1) by more than 0.5% within a quarter signals a weakening economy, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of GDPC1 decrease.
